name: Camp 7 Lake Campground
evidence: rec.gov 232318 tags RV sites 022-031 'Lakefront', but satellite z19 with RIDB site points shows their pad clearings ~55 m from Camp Seven Lake behind continuous forest on a slope (pads 240-244 m vs lake 228 m DEM): view, not on-water; old pin was at the day-use beach, re-pinned to the loop

name: Camp Deer Trails
evidence: Campspot sells 'Rustic waterfront' (7 sites, to 30 ft) only to vans/trailers/fifth-wheels, not motorhomes; operator map (overview only) puts Stag Ridge S1-S16 near Long Lake; satellite z18: electric loop ~140 m from the lake behind trees, Stag Ridge under canopy on the bluff; no counting source. Stored pin is on the campground (Campspot point is the entrance)

name: Burton's Landing State Forest Campground
evidence: satellite (Esri z18/z19 + Bing z18/z19): camp road with parked campers ~100-110 m S of the Au Sable behind a continuous forest band; the riverside meadow and the canoe-landing loop hold no pads; old pin was the river landing, re-pinned to the camp road

name: Burned Dam Campground
evidence: satellite z18/z19 (leaf-off) at FS pin 46.3138,-89.0531: campground clearing beside Mex-i-mine Falls, ~20-60 m from the Middle Branch Ontonagon behind a wooded riverbank strip; no pads legible at the water and no per-site map; FS 'river access' is not site evidence; defaults down

name: Carp River Campground
evidence: rec.gov 234083 catalog: none of the 20 sites carries a Proximity to Water flag; satellite z18/z19 with RIDB site points: full canopy, nearest sites (009, 012) 25-30 m above the ravine of the Carp River, which FS says is reached by stairs down the bank (climb-down)

name: CreationView Campground
evidence: operator overview map draws a site block by Otto's Pond and only a trail to Mud (Nature) Lake; satellite z18/z19: pond ringed by trees except an open lawn on its SW side with no pads, nearest visible RV ~30 m away through trees; CampLife's Water-front tag is on the cabin type only; no counting source

name: East Branch of Fox River State Forest Campground
evidence: satellite z17-z19: the DNR-pin clearing at King's Pond holds a shelter (fishing-pier access) ~30 m from the pond through trees; site spurs to the south sit under canopy near the East Branch with no pads legible at the water; no per-site map exists; DNR prose is not site evidence; defaults down

name: Fort Wilkins Historic State Park — East Loop
evidence: DNR East Campground map: sites 1-10 line Lake Fanny Hooe with overlook decks and 'stairs to lake'; satellite z19: those pads ~20-25 m from the shore behind a thin tree fringe, ~7 m above the lake (DEM 195 vs 188), so a climb-down bank: view, not on-water; old pin was in the West campground, re-pinned to the East loop
